title: A Twin-Turboprop With a Built-In Type Rating? Propair Cheyenne III | MSFS 2024 Marketplace
description:
Are you looking to expand your virtual hangar in Microsoft Flight Simulator 2024 this week, or are you deciding which new Marketplace add-ons are actually worth your hard-earned cash? Today's marketplace drop delivers high-performance corporate executive travel and rugged alpine rotorcraft operations, spanning twin-turboprop training workflows to high-visibility mountain rescue liveries! Whether you are looking to earn a full virtual type rating aboard Propair Flight's Piper Cheyenne III or navigate tight alpine valleys with HR SimYard's H125 Italian Livery Pack 2, this focused update has plenty to explore.

In this marketplace breakdown, we take a close look at features, panel variants, realistic expectations, and new releases across the MSFS 2024 virtual flight line:

✈️ CORPORATE TURBOPROPS & VIRTUAL TYPE RATINGS
We kick things off with a standout addition to the marketplace ramp: the Piper Cheyenne III by Propair Flight. Powered by twin PT6A turboprops, this package features analog cockpit instrumentation with authentic cockpit wear-and-tear, executive passenger cabins, and dedicated air ambulance medevac configurations. The headline feature, however, is the bundled SkyPass virtual type rating program—providing a structured training progression covering ground school, aircraft systems, telemetry-monitored handling, and check flights with 100 included evaluation credits. We look at its visual modeling, systems layout, and career mode compatibility.

🚁 ALPINE ROTORCRAFT UTILITY
Looking to take the native Asobo H125 into demanding high-altitude operations?

HR SimYard H125 Italian Livery Pack Vol. 2: A focused collection of authentic Italian commercial, mountain logistics, and aerial work colorways. We inspect the high-visibility schemes including Air Service Center, EliFriulia, Air Green, and Elikos/Star Work Sky for operations across the Italian Alps and Dolomites.

Which of these new add-ons are you loading onto the ramp first? Cruising cross-country in the Cheyenne III while working through your SkyPass rating, or slinging loads through the Dolomites in the H125? Let us know in the comments below!

If you find these marketplace breakdowns helpful, don't forget to hit that like button, subscribe for weekly flight sim coverage, and clear skies on your next flight!
